Summary
: This essay in English studies the Dramatic plays authored by Bhasa, who is celebrated as the earliest Sanskrit dramatist and was praised by others, including Kalidasa, Banabhatta, Vamana, and Rajashekhara. He is dated earlier than Kalidasa, plausibly 4th-5th century BCE. This study primarily focuses on a publication of thirteen plays (called the “Bhasa Nataka Chakra”). There are five chapters which reconstructs his socio-cultural history through six of his Dramas via comparative analysis with the Mahabharata and texts like Venisamhara. Overall, Bhasa’s Mahabharata dramas are treated as key documents for understanding refined ancient Indian civilization and epic influence on lived culture.
